rationale: Consecutive RT-PCR-confirmed patients with chemosensory dysfunction followed 4 years with multivariate regression; taste was self-reported tVAS only with no objective gustatory test, and follow-up fell from 83 at baseline to 34 at 1 year and 26 at 4 years with no incomplete-follow-up strategy.

rationale: Prospective consecutive sample of children undergoing PCR testing with a pre-recruitment power calculation, but only 51 of 205 approached completed testing and taste was a single screening-questionnaire item (objective testing assessed smell only), a measurement concern.

rationale: One-year follow-up of the COCOS cohort with validated Taste Strip Test plus VAS and drop-outs (36 of 113) described and compared with participants; the cohort had olfactory disorder at entry by design and no confounding strategy for the prognostic analysis was reported.

domain_summary: JBI cohort 8/10 applicable Yes (Q1 Yes; Q2 Yes; Q3 Yes; Q4 Yes; Q5 Yes; Q6 No; Q7 Unclear; Q8 Yes; Q9 Yes; Q10 NA; Q11 Yes)
rationale: Consecutive laboratory-confirmed mild COVID-19 patients with gustatory dysfunction from four hospitals, 701 of 718 completing at least 60 days' follow-up and a multivariate analysis addressing confounders; taste recovery was self-reported by questionnaire with no objective testing (authors' stated limitation), a measurement concern weighed but not rated High alone, and recruitment via ENT clinics may introduce selection bias.
